case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.holding: The court reversed termination, holding that both a statutory ground and best interest must be shown by clear and convincing evidence and that permanency-plan requirements supporting a substantial-noncompliance ground must be reasonable and related to the conditions necessitating foster care.
key_cases.relevance: Supplies the evidentiary threshold whose failure requires dismissal of a termination petition.
key_cases.quote: To terminate parental rights, a court must determine that clear and convincing evidence proves not only that statutory grounds exist but also that termination is in the child's best interest.

key_cases.holding: The court reversed termination, holding that the petitioners failed to prove by clear and convincing evidence that terminating the mother's parental rights was in the children's best interests.
key_cases.relevance: Shows a termination petition failing and the case ending without severance of the parental relationship.
key_cases.quote: We conclude that Father and Stepmother failed to prove by clear and convincing evidence that termination of Mother's parental rights is in the best interests of the children.

key_cases.case_name: In re Adoption of Angela E.
key_cases.holding: The court held that a prior order suspending the father's visitation did not prevent a finding that his failure to visit was willful, sustained abandonment by willful failure to visit, rejected abandonment by failure to support, and remanded for a best-interest determination.
key_cases.relevance: Shows an appellate court sustaining one abandonment ground while rejecting another, leaving best interest undecided on remand.
key_cases.quote: We agree with the Court of Appeals that the prior order suspending Father's visitation rights did not preclude a finding that Father willfully failed to visit the children.

key_cases.holding: The court reinstated the trial court's refusal to terminate, holding that the statutory best-interest factors are weighed according to the facts of each case and that the combined proof did not clearly and convincingly show termination was in the children's best interests.
key_cases.relevance: Explains when a termination petition must be dismissed for failure of the best-interest proof.
key_cases.quote: the facts and circumstances of each unique case dictate how weighty and relevant each statutory factor is in the context of the case

key_cases.holding: The court reversed and remanded for a new hearing, holding that a termination order must contain the findings of fact and conclusions of law required by Tenn. Code Ann. sec. 36-1-113(c) and (k) even where the parent consents, and that an appellate court cannot review the decision without them.
key_cases.relevance: Requires that a termination judgment rest on stated findings, so a petition resolved without them cannot stand and the case returns to the trial court.
key_cases.quote: We may not conduct de novo review of the termination decision in the absence of such findings.
